title: Paul Ash and the Oriental Theater: Norville becomes Norvo
summary: Jack Tebo gets him a single with Paul Ash on the Publix circuit; when Ash garbles his name Variety prints Red Norvo, and he keeps it.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: And I really always wanted to write, all those early years, when I was -- when I later became a single in vaudeville, I made a-- quite a bit of money doing a single. The same Jack Tiboo got me with Paul Ash on the [Publix] Circuit and I was working a single, I was maybe 18-19 years old. 19 I guess. Maybe before I was 20 -- I know the years I'm not sure --
-- I don't know when did this stop or that stop, really. --
-- but I know I opened the Oriental Theater
in Chicago with Paul Ash, the first week.

And I was just a thing thing that was on a platform at the finish, but the following week, I was there for two or three weeks, I played a solo, that's when my name was changed, Paul Ash couldn't remember my name. He called me Norvick, hecalled me Norman, and he called meeverything and finally, variety, the day -- view -- reviewed the show the second week, he called me Red Norvo. And that's the way it is. So this Jack Tihoo said, looks like you're going to have trouble. So I said, 'Well, change it if youwant to.'
Norville is what the -- my real name.
Was my real name. So, I just kept that.
And it was a great write-up, so he felt that that would be a good thing.
